pos.personaBrief: La Máquina's stated aim was to have the ball, with short passing (La Página Millonaria), seven-pass moves and 'fútbol de lujo' (Juvenal 1943); Muñoz says they took the ball and played in midfield rather than rushing at goal.

pro.personaBrief: River started moves from the back with precise passing (La Página Millonaria), and the inside-forwards dropped to build with the half-backs in the 'cuadrado mágico' (Juvenal 1942); his 1965 call to 'hacer caminar la pelota' and against 'bordados' makes him less patient than a pure build-up coach.

est.personaBrief: The forwards 'se desmarcan, cambian de posiciones' (Juvenal), Pedernera became a dropping false nine (FIFA), and roles were found in free 'fútbol loco' sessions. Wingers were the exception: he wanted them on the touchline ('la raya a la espalda', 'mande los punteros contra la raya').

lar.personaBrief: Two true wingers (Muñoz, Deambrosi, then Loustau; Juvenal). He moved Muñoz and Loustau out to the wing himself, and in 1965 he said 'Debe preocupar el ancho... Mande los punteros contra la raya. Oblíguelos a desbordar.'

blo.personaBrief: No pressing evidence (a gap dimension). The 1940s W-M River team had five forwards, won games by out-passing opponents and defended through man-markers like Yácono, so I judge it did not press high and did not sit in a deep compact block either.

mar.personaBrief: The only marking facts are individual: Yácono's 'marca pegajosa' and his role as 'specialist man-marker' (Wilson, El Gráfico, Jensen). This fits the man-oriented marking that was normal in the 1940s W-M.

pla.personaBrief: No verified evidence; these answers come from general knowledge. They follow his stated view: 'yo soy el que impongo los principios', every youth division should have 'la misma fisonomía de fútbol', and he claimed La Máquina was 'perfecta'. That points to a coach who backs his own model over opponent study, though he also shaped roles around the players he found (Loustau, Muñoz).

res.personaBrief: The team's behaviour was spectacle ('fútbol de lujo', 'Knights of Anguish'), but his belief in 1965 was blunt: 'la única verdad es ganar... Basta de lujos, basta de bordados.' I weigh both, so he puts the result first while keeping an attacking side.

sis.personaBrief: 'Al jugador lo construyo yo' and 'Al jugador lo hace quien lo conduce' show a coach who believes the system makes the player, and he wanted 'espíritu de sacrificio' from everyone. He still gave freedom to stars like Pedernera ('el director') and Sívori ('diez desconocidos... después lo pongo a Sívori').

jog.personaBrief: La Máquina was technical, but his own belief in 1965 was 'FISICO, AGUANTE, VELOCIDAD, ESPIRITU DE SACRIFICIO' and 'Qué me importa el hábil si no tiene los otros atributos'. He wanted physical players in the central positions and sent small players to the wings. Behaviour still keeps him away from pure duel football.

bas.personaBrief: He backed 19-year-old Loustau, released free by Racing, over buying Arregui for 70,000 pesos. He brought Sívori to River at 16, and said in 1965 that 'puede aparecer en la primera un chico de la cuarta'. Loustau broke into the 1942 title side.

lid.personaBrief: Known as 'La Biblia del fútbol' for his authority (Wikipedia). In 1965 he said assistants who disagree 'se tendrá que ir' and that 'yo soy el que impongo los principios'. The free 'fútbol loco' sessions and Peucelle's suggestion show some openness, but not a shared command.
